intent.raw_query: Iceland Northern Lights and hot springs, $3500 couple, January

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunting Tour
experiences.description: Join a guided evening tour away from Reykjavik's light pollution to witness the aurora borealis dancing across the sky. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science behind this natural phenomenon while capturing stunning photographs.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and swim-up bars while surrounded by dramatic lava fields. Book the Comfort package for access to the main lagoon, towel rental, and one silica mud mask.

experiences.name: Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure
experiences.description: Snorkel or dive between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates in crystal-clear glacial water with visibility up to 100 meters. The surreal blue and green hues of the water make this one of the most unique natural experiences on Earth, guided by certified instructors.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring
experiences.description: Relax in Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a naturally heated geothermal pool surrounded by bubbling hot springs and a small geyser that erupts every few minutes. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic experience offers a peaceful soak amid stunning Icelandic countryside.

experiences.name: Skaftafell Glacier Hike on Vatnajökull
experiences.description: Strap on crampons and hike across Europe's largest glacier with an expert guide. Explore stunning ice formations, deep blue crevasses, and ash layers from ancient volcanic eruptions. The hike offers breathtaking panoramic views of the surrounding black sand plains and mountain peaks.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Iceland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 06:10. Clear customs and collect luggage. Take the Flybus or a budget shuttle to Reykjavik BSI terminal, then arrange onward travel north toward Siglufjörður. The drive is approximately 4-5 hours via Route 1 and the Héðinsfjörður tunnel — consider renting a budget compact car at the airport for the full trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the scenic drive north through the Tröllaskagi peninsula. Stop briefly at Akureyri if needed for groceries or fuel. Arrive in Siglufjörður in the early afternoon. Check in to Hotel Siglunes on Lækjargata 10 and settle into your room. Take a short walk along the harbor to get oriented with the charming fishing village.
day_by_day.evening: Rest and recover from travel. Take a gentle evening stroll along the waterfront and scan the sky for the northern lights — Siglufjörður's low light pollution makes it an excellent viewing spot. Bundle up warmly and watch from the harbor pier.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or coffee at Keflavik Airport before departure — budget around 1,000-1,500 ISK
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches or stop at a petrol station N1 or Orkan along Route 1 for a hot dog (pylsur) — Iceland's iconic budget meal at around 500-700 ISK
meals.dinner: Kaffi Rauðka in Siglufjörður — a cozy local café offering affordable soup and bread or fish dishes, budget around 2,500-3,500 ISK

day_by_day.notes: January days are very short in northern Iceland — expect only about 4-5 hours of daylight. Road conditions can be challenging; check road.is before and during your drive. Dress in warm layers. Pick up groceries in Akureyri or Ólafsfjörður to save money on meals during your stay.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið) in Siglufjörður, one of Iceland's most acclaimed regional museums. It tells the fascinating story of the town's herring boom in the early 20th century. Entry is around 2,000 ISK — check if it's open in January as hours may be reduced.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the colorful streets and old wooden houses of Siglufjörður on foot. Walk up toward the ski slopes area above town for panoramic views of the fjord and surrounding snow-capped mountains. The Siglufjörður ski resort (Skíðasvæðið) is one of Iceland's best and lift tickets are relatively affordable if you wish to ski.
day_by_day.evening: Northern lights hunt from the hillside above town or along the fjord shore. The mountains surrounding Siglufjörður create a dramatic backdrop for aurora viewing. Check aurora forecast on vedur.is and head out if the KP index is favorable.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the hotel — oatmeal, bread, and coffee from groceries purchased the day before
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from hotel — sandwiches with Icelandic skyr and fruit
meals.dinner: Prepare a simple pasta or soup meal in the hotel kitchen if available, or visit Kaffi Rauðka for a budget bowl of lamb soup (kjötsúpa) — around 2,000-2,500 ISK

day_by_day.notes: January is peak northern lights season in northern Iceland. Download the Vedur app for real-time aurora forecasts. Siglufjörður sits at 66°N latitude, giving excellent aurora viewing opportunities. Dress in full winter gear including thermal base layers, waterproof outer shell, hat, gloves, and warm boots.

day_by_day.morning: Drive through the Héðinsfjörður tunnel (free) to the neighboring village of Ólafsfjörður. Explore this quiet fishing village and walk along its harbor. The drive through the tunnel and the fjord scenery is stunning even in winter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue driving south along the Tröllaskagi peninsula on Route 82 toward Dalvík. Stop at viewpoints along the way to photograph the dramatic mountain and fjord scenery. Visit Dalvík briefly — a small fishing town with a quirky Giant Museum (Byggðasafnið Hvoll) if open.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður via the tunnel. Spend the evening in the hotel warming up with hot drinks. If skies are clear, head out for another northern lights attempt from the harbor or hillside.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel — eggs, bread, and Icelandic skyr
meals.lunch: Stop at a petrol station or small café in Ólafsfjörður or Dalvík — hot dog and coffee for around 800-1,200 ISK
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at hotel — cook a simple fish or chicken dish using groceries from Akureyri

day_by_day.notes: Route 82 along the Tröllaskagi peninsula is one of Iceland's most scenic drives. Check road conditions at road.is before departing. The Héðinsfjörður tunnel connects Siglufjörður and Ólafsfjörður and is free to use. Total driving for the day is approximately 80-100 km.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south to Akureyri (approximately 1 hour from Siglufjörður). Explore Iceland's second-largest city. Visit the iconic Akureyrarkirkja church perched on the hill — free to enter. Walk the main shopping street Hafnarstræti and browse local shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Akureyri Botanical Garden (Lystigarðurinn) — free entry and beautiful even in winter with snow-covered grounds. Explore the Akureyri Art Museum (Listasafnið á Akureyri) if budget allows (around 1,500 ISK). Stock up on groceries at Bónus or Krónan supermarket — the cheapest options in Iceland.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Siglufjörður. Stop along Route 1 or Route 82 at a dark spot for northern lights viewing on the way back. The skies between Akureyri and Siglufjörður are often very dark and clear.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Bónus supermarket in Akureyri — pick up ready-made sandwiches or visit Akureyri's famous hot dog stand for a budget meal around 600-1,000 ISK
meals.dinner: Greifinn restaurant in Akureyri offers affordable pizza and pasta — budget around 2,500-3,500 ISK, or self-cater back at the hotel

day_by_day.notes: Akureyri is the main hub for supplies in northern Iceland. Stock up on groceries, medications, and any gear you need. Bónus (yellow pig logo) is the most budget-friendly supermarket. The drive back to Siglufjörður takes about 1 hour on Route 82 — allow extra time in winter conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Lake Mývatn area (approximately 1.5 hours east of Akureyri on Route 1). Visit the dramatic Dimmuborgir lava formations — a free, otherworldly landscape of twisted lava pillars and arches. Walk the marked trails through the formations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Mývatn Nature Baths (Jarðböðin við Mývatn) — a geothermal hot spring lagoon similar to the Blue Lagoon but far less crowded and more affordable at around 5,500 ISK. Soak in the milky blue geothermal waters surrounded by volcanic landscape. Also explore the Hverfjall volcanic crater rim (free) if time and conditions allow.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Siglufjörður. The Mývatn area is excellent for northern lights due to minimal light pollution. Consider stopping on the return journey at a dark roadside spot to watch for auroras before arriving back at the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel before early departure
meals.lunch: Bring a packed lunch from the hotel to eat at Dimmuborgir — save money by avoiding the Mývatn area restaurants
meals.dinner: Gamli Bærinn café near Mývatn for affordable soup and bread (around 2,000-2,500 ISK) before the drive back, or self-cater at hotel

day_by_day.notes: The Mývatn Nature Baths are one of the best budget alternatives to the Blue Lagoon. Bring your swimsuit and towel (or rent one for around 700 ISK). The total round trip from Siglufjörður is approximately 3-3.5 hours of driving — start early to maximize daylight. Road conditions on Route 1 in January can be icy; drive carefully.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Siglufjörður ski resort (Skíðasvæðið á Siglufirði) — one of Iceland's oldest and most charming ski areas located right above the town. Day lift passes are relatively affordable compared to European resorts (around 5,000-7,000 ISK). Even if you don't ski, the views from the slopes over the fjord are spectacular.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Folk Music Center (Þjóðlagasetur) in Siglufjörður if open — a small museum dedicated to Icelandic folk music traditions. Walk along the old harbor area and photograph the colorful fishing boats and warehouses. Explore the old fish processing buildings along the waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Northern lights vigil from the ski slope area above town — the elevation gives a wider sky view. Bring a thermos of hot chocolate and warm blankets. Check the aurora forecast and cloud cover on vedur.is before heading out.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel — porridge with Icelandic honey and coffee
meals.lunch: Ski resort café if available, or packed lunch from hotel
meals.dinner: Kaffi Rauðka in Siglufjörður — try the fish of the day (dagurinn fiskur) which is usually the most affordable fresh option, around 2,500-3,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Siglufjörður's ski resort is a hidden gem — small, uncrowded, and authentic. The town itself is one of Iceland's most photogenic in winter with snow-covered rooftops and colorful houses. January is typically the snowiest month, making conditions ideal for winter activities.

day_by_day.morning: Drive north along the coast toward Hofsós (approximately 45 minutes south of Siglufjörður on Route 76). Visit the Icelandic Emigration Center (Vesturfarasetrið) — a fascinating museum about Icelanders who emigrated to North America in the 19th century (check winter opening hours).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Hofsós Swimming Pool — one of Iceland's most beautifully situated geothermal pools, perched on a cliff overlooking Skagafjörður fjord with views of distant mountains. Entry is very affordable at around 1,000-1,200 ISK. Swim in the outdoor geothermal pool with stunning winter scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Siglufjörður via Route 76. Stop at Sauðárkrókur briefly if needed for supplies. Return to hotel and spend the evening watching for northern lights from the harbor.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Hofsós harbor with fjord views
meals.dinner: Self-catered at hotel — cook a hearty lamb stew (kjötsúpa) using Icelandic lamb from the supermarket

day_by_day.notes: The Hofsós pool is one of Iceland's most Instagram-worthy swimming pools but remains largely off the tourist trail. In January it may have limited hours — call ahead or check online. The drive along Route 76 through Skagafjörður offers beautiful winter scenery. Total driving for the day is approximately 90-100 km.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Varmahlíð in Skagafjörður valley (approximately 1 hour from Siglufjörður). Visit the Glaumbær turf farm museum — one of Iceland's best-preserved traditional turf farmhouses, offering a glimpse into 18th and 19th century Icelandic rural life. Entry around 2,000 ISK (check winter hours).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Skagafjörður valley — known as Iceland's horse country. Drive along the valley floor and observe Icelandic horses in their natural winter habitat. Stop at the Víðimýrarkirkja turf church near Varmahlíð — a beautifully preserved historic church that is free to view from outside.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður. The drive back through the mountains offers excellent northern lights viewing opportunities if skies are clear. Stop at a dark roadside pullout on Route 76 for aurora watching.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Café at Glaumbær museum (Áss café) — affordable soup and traditional Icelandic pancakes (pönnukökur) around 1,500-2,000 ISK
meals.dinner: Self-catered at hotel — pasta with Icelandic lamb mince sauce

day_by_day.notes: Glaumbær is one of Iceland's most important cultural heritage sites. The turf farmhouse complex is remarkably well preserved. Skagafjörður is famous for Icelandic horse breeding — you may see herds of horses in the snowy fields. The valley is also known for its Viking Age history.

day_by_day.morning: Full day trip to the Snæfellsnes Peninsula area — this is a long drive (approximately 4-5 hours one way from Siglufjörður) so consider whether to do this as an overnight or a very long day trip. Alternatively, explore closer to home: hike up the valley behind Siglufjörður toward the mountain pass Hestskarð for panoramic winter views.
day_by_day.afternoon: If staying local: snowshoe or hike along the frozen valley floor behind Siglufjörður. The mountains surrounding the town offer dramatic winter hiking with proper gear. Visit the old avalanche defense structures above town — Siglufjörður has been historically affected by avalanches and the protective earthworks are impressive.
day_by_day.evening: Dedicated northern lights photography session. Set up at the harbor with a tripod if you have one. The reflection of auroras in the calm fjord waters creates spectacular photo opportunities. Stay out until midnight if the forecast is good.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel — eggs and toast with Icelandic butter
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the hillside hike — thermos of soup and sandwiches
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a slightly nicer dinner at Kaffi Rauðka — try the Arctic char (bleikja) if available, budget around 3,000-4,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: January is statistically one of the best months for northern lights in Iceland due to long dark nights. The KP index needs to be at least 2-3 for visible auroras, and cloud cover must be minimal. Check vedur.is multiple times daily. Siglufjörður's position in a deep fjord means you need to get to higher ground or the fjord mouth for the best sky views.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Akureyri for a more thorough exploration. Visit the Akureyri Museum (Minjasafnið á Akureyri) — a regional history museum with affordable entry around 1,500 ISK. Explore the old town area with its historic wooden houses.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Nonnahús museum — the childhood home of beloved Icelandic author Jón Sveinsson (Nonni), a charming historic wooden house. Walk along the Akureyri waterfront and visit the Christmas Garden (Jólahúsið) — a year-round Christmas shop that is free to browse. Explore the geothermal swimming pool Sundlaug Akureyrar — one of Iceland's best public pools at around 1,000 ISK entry.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Siglufjörður. Stop at the Vaðlaheiði viewpoint on Route 1 north of Akureyri for a panoramic view over Eyjafjörður — excellent northern lights viewing spot on clear nights.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Bláa Kannan café in Akureyri — affordable coffee and pastries, or grab a hot dog from the nearby stand, budget 800-1,500 ISK
meals.dinner: Strikið restaurant in Akureyri has a budget lunch menu that sometimes extends to early dinner — or try Hamborgarabúllan for affordable burgers around 2,000-2,500 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Akureyri's geothermal pool is a great budget activity — locals swim year-round and it's a wonderful cultural experience. The pool has hot tubs, steam rooms, and a waterslide. Bring your own towel to avoid the rental fee. Stock up on any remaining groceries at Bónus before heading back.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Tröllaskagi peninsula's eastern side — drive through the Ólafsfjörður tunnel and continue south along Route 82 toward Grenivík. The coastal road offers dramatic views of Eyjafjörður with Akureyri visible across the water. Stop at scenic viewpoints for photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Laufás historic turf farm near Grenivík — a beautifully preserved 19th century turf farmhouse and church overlooking Eyjafjörður (check winter opening hours, may be closed). Even if closed, the exterior and setting are worth the drive. Continue to Grenivík village for a short walk along the harbor.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður via Akureyri and Route 82. This is your second-to-last full day in the area — spend the evening packing non-essentials and doing a final northern lights watch from your favorite spot in Siglufjörður.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from hotel eaten at Laufás or Grenivík harbor
meals.dinner: Final self-catered dinner at hotel — use up remaining groceries to minimize waste and cost

day_by_day.notes: The Tröllaskagi peninsula loop via Ólafsfjörður, Dalvík, and Grenivík is one of northern Iceland's most scenic drives. Total loop distance is approximately 150-180 km. Road conditions in January can be challenging — check road.is. This is a good day to take your time and enjoy the winter landscape without rushing.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Siglufjörður. Take a slow farewell walk through the town — photograph the harbor, the colorful houses, and the snow-covered mountains one last time. Visit any local spots you may have missed during your stay. Check out of Hotel Siglunes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the drive south toward Reykjavik (approximately 5-6 hours). Stop in Akureyri for a final lunch and any last-minute shopping. Continue south on Route 1 through the dramatic highland interior or coastal route. Stop at Goðafoss waterfall — one of Iceland's most beautiful waterfalls, free to visit and accessible right off Route 1.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Reykjavik. Check into a budget hostel such as Kex Hostel, Loft Hostel, or Bus Hostel (book in advance, dorm beds from 4,000-6,000 ISK). Explore the Laugavegur main street and Hallgrímskirkja church area in the evening.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel — final use of remaining food supplies
meals.lunch: Akureyri — Noodle Station for affordable Asian noodle soup around 1,800-2,200 ISK, one of the best budget options in Iceland
meals.dinner: Reykjavik — Hlöllabátar (Icelandic submarine sandwiches) on Laugavegur for around 1,500-2,000 ISK, or Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur hot dog stand for the classic Icelandic hot dog experience

day_by_day.notes: Goðafoss waterfall is located right off Route 1 near Fosshóll — it's free, accessible, and stunning even in winter with ice formations. Allow 30-45 minutes for the stop. The drive from Akureyri to Reykjavik is approximately 4.5-5 hours — start early enough to arrive before dark. Book Reykjavik accommodation well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Reykjavik on a budget. Visit Hallgrímskirkja church — free to enter the church, tower elevator costs around 1,000 ISK for panoramic city views. Walk down Skólavörðustígur street to Laugavegur. Visit the Harpa Concert Hall — free to walk through the stunning glass architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Settlement Exhibition (Landnámssýningin) — an underground museum built around a Viking Age longhouse discovered beneath the city, entry around 2,200 ISK. Walk along the Sæbraut coastal path for views of Mount Esja and the bay. Visit the Sun Voyager (Sólfar) sculpture on the waterfront — free. Return rental car if not already done (return to Keflavik airport area).
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Iceland. Head to the Reykjavik city center for a farewell dinner. If budget allows, try Icelandic fish and chips at Reykjavik Fish (Fiskfélagið takeaway) for around 2,500-3,000 ISK. Pack bags and prepare for early morning departure. Check in online for your return flight.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast if included, or grab a pastry and coffee at Brauð & Co bakery on Frakkastígur — excellent Icelandic sourdough and pastries around 800-1,200 ISK
meals.lunch: Reykjavik Roasters café for coffee and a light lunch, or Hlöllabátar for another affordable sandwich around 1,500-2,000 ISK
meals.dinner: Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur hot dog stand — the most iconic budget meal in Iceland at around 500-700 ISK per hot dog, or Noodle Station Reykjavik for a warming bowl of noodle soup

day_by_day.notes: If your return flight is early on January 29th, arrange a Flybus or airport transfer the night before or very early morning — book in advance at re.is. The Flybus from BSI terminal to Keflavik takes approximately 45-50 minutes. Budget approximately 3,500-4,000 ISK for the Flybus. Leave extra time for airport security in January. Return your rental car with a full tank of fuel to avoid expensive refueling charges from the rental company.

trip_options.title: Classic Iceland Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Keflavik International Airport at 06:10. Clear customs and collect luggage. Pick up pre-booked rental car (4WD recommended for winter driving). Grab a coffee and light breakfast at the airport café before beginning the long drive north to Siglufjörður (approx. 5–6 hours depending on road conditions and stops).
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop in Akureyri (Iceland's second city) around midday for a stretch and lunch. Explore the charming town center briefly — walk down Hafnarstræti, peek at the iconic Akureyrarkirkja church from the outside. Continue the final 45-minute drive north through the stunning Héðinsfjörður tunnel system to Siglufjörður. Check in to Hotel Siglunes and settle into your room.
day_by_day.evening: Rest and recover from travel. Take a short evening stroll along Siglufjörður's quiet harbor front to get your bearings. Dine at the hotel restaurant or a nearby local spot. Early night to reset your body clock.

meals.breakfast: Airport café at Keflavik — grab a skyr yogurt pot, pastry, and coffee (budget ~1,500–2,000 ISK)
meals.lunch: Rub23 or Strikið restaurant in Akureyri — fresh fish of the day or lamb soup (budget ~2,500–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes restaurant — try the Arctic char or lamb shank with local vegetables (budget ~4,000–5,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Road conditions in January can be severe — check road.is before and during the drive. The Héðinsfjörður tunnel (Héðinsfjarðargöng) may have restrictions in bad weather. Keep emergency supplies in the car. Daylight in January is very limited (roughly 5–6 hours), so the drive will be mostly in darkness. Drive carefully and do not rush.

day_by_day.morning: After a proper rest, enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast. Then visit the Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið) — one of Iceland's finest regional museums, telling the story of Siglufjörður's booming herring industry. Fascinating exhibits and well worth the 1,500 ISK entry fee.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or walk to the edge of town and explore the dramatic fjord scenery on foot. The Siglufjörður valley offers short winter walks along the fjord shore. Visit the local swimming pool (Sundlaug Siglufjarðar) — a classic Icelandic geothermal community pool with hot pots, perfect for warming up and meeting locals.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights watch from the harbor or hillside above town. Siglufjörður has very little light pollution and is an excellent spot for aurora viewing. Download the Vedur aurora forecast app and head out if the KP index is favorable. Wrap up warm with multiple layers.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — full Icelandic breakfast with skyr, eggs, smoked salmon, and rye bread
meals.lunch: Café Rauðka in Siglufjörður — homemade soup, open-faced sandwiches, and coffee (budget ~2,000–2,800 ISK)
meals.dinner: Hannes Boy restaurant in Siglufjörður — local fish dishes and Icelandic lamb (budget ~3,500–5,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Herring Era Museum may have reduced winter hours — confirm opening times in advance. The community pool is a wonderful authentic Icelandic experience and costs around 1,000 ISK. Aurora activity is unpredictable; patience and clear skies are essential. January offers long dark nights, maximizing aurora viewing windows.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip east along the Tröllaskagi peninsula. Drive the scenic Route 76 toward Hofsós. Stop at viewpoints overlooking the fjords and mountains. Visit the Hofsós Swimming Pool — arguably Iceland's most beautifully situated geothermal pool, perched on a cliff edge above the fjord with panoramic views (open year-round).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Sauðárkrókur, the largest town in the Skagafjörður region. Visit the Skagafjörður Heritage Museum (Byggðasafn Skagfirðinga) to learn about the region's horse-breeding culture and Viking history. Browse the small town center and grab supplies at the local supermarket (Krónan or Bónus).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður before dark (aim to be back by 16:00 as roads can be treacherous after dark in winter). Relax at the hotel. Another aurora watch opportunity from the hotel or harbor area if skies are clear.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — full breakfast included
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or café stop in Hofsós — local bakery items and thermos coffee (budget ~1,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes restaurant — try the pan-fried cod with butter sauce or the vegetarian option (budget ~4,000–5,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Hofsós pool is a hidden gem — arrive early to avoid any crowds. Route 76 is scenic but can be icy; drive with extreme caution. Check road.is before departing. The Tröllaskagi peninsula is one of Iceland's most dramatic and undervisited regions — enjoy the solitude.

day_by_day.morning: Drive west to Akureyri (approx. 45 minutes). Spend the morning exploring Iceland's northern capital properly. Walk the pedestrian shopping street Hafnarstræti, visit the Botanical Garden (Lystigarðurinn — free entry, beautiful even in winter), and admire the Akureyrarkirkja church up close.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Akureyri Art Museum (Listasafnið á Akureyri) for rotating contemporary Icelandic art exhibitions. Then head to the Akureyri Swimming Pool (Sundlaug Akureyrar) — a large geothermal complex with multiple hot pots, steam rooms, and a waterslide. A perfect mid-trip relaxation stop.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in Akureyri before returning to Siglufjörður. Akureyri has the best restaurant selection in northern Iceland. Return to hotel by 20:00.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — full breakfast
meals.lunch: Bautinn restaurant in Akureyri — traditional Icelandic lamb soup and fresh bread (budget ~2,500–3,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Strikið restaurant in Akureyri — elevated Icelandic cuisine with fjord views; try the reindeer or Arctic char (budget ~5,000–7,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Akureyri is a worthwhile day trip with genuine city amenities. The Botanical Garden is surprisingly interesting even in winter with its hardy Arctic plants. Parking in Akureyri town center is free for the first hour. The drive back to Siglufjörður in the dark requires care — take it slowly through the tunnels.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated aurora and nature day. Sleep in slightly to rest. After breakfast, take a guided snowshoe or winter walk in the mountains above Siglufjörður (arrange through the hotel or local guide services). The valley above town offers stunning winter wilderness scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the local ski area — Siglufjörður has a small but charming ski hill (Skíðasvæðið á Siglufirði) with a few runs and a ski lift. Even if you don't ski, the views from the top are spectacular. Rent equipment locally if desired (budget ~5,000–8,000 ISK for rental and lift pass).
day_by_day.evening: Dedicated Northern Lights Hunting Tour — book a guided evening tour from Siglufjörður or nearby Akureyri. A local guide will drive you to the best dark-sky locations based on that night's aurora forecast and cloud cover. This is your best chance for a memorable aurora experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — full breakfast
meals.lunch: Ski area café or packed lunch from hotel — hot soup in a thermos, sandwiches, and chocolate (budget ~1,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Hannes Boy restaurant — celebrate the aurora hunt with a hearty dinner; try the fish stew or lamb chops (budget ~4,000–5,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Northern Lights tour in advance — local operators in Akureyri include Arctic Adventures and local Siglufjörður guides. Tours typically run 21:00–01:00. Dress in your warmest layers — standing outside in January in northern Iceland is extremely cold. Hand warmers are highly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery morning after the late aurora tour. Leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Visit the Siglufjörður Folk Music Center (Þjóðlagasetur) — a charming museum dedicated to Icelandic folk music traditions, housed in a historic building.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive the dramatic Route 82 around the Tröllaskagi peninsula toward Ólafsfjörður and Dalvík. Stop at scenic viewpoints along the coast. Visit Dalvík and take the short ferry crossing to Hrísey island — Iceland's second-largest island, known for its birdlife and peaceful atmosphere (ferry runs year-round, ~30 min crossing).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður via Akureyri. Stop for groceries if needed. Quiet evening at the hotel — enjoy the hot tub if available, or relax with a book and a glass of wine.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — full breakfast (eat slowly and enjoy the rest)
meals.lunch: Café or bakery in Dalvík — fish and chips or lamb burger (budget ~2,000–2,800 ISK)
meals.dinner: Self-catered or hotel restaurant — pick up fresh ingredients from Akureyri supermarket for a simple pasta or salad (budget ~2,000–3,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Check the Hrísey ferry schedule in advance (Sævar ferry service). The island is very quiet in January but the walk around it is peaceful and the birdwatching can be rewarding. Route 82 around the peninsula is scenic but can be challenging in winter — check road conditions. This is a good rest-and-explore day.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the drive south toward the Golden Circle and central Iceland (approx. 5–6 hours to Reykjavik area). This is a travel day — depart early to maximize daylight. Drive south on Route 1 (Ring Road) through the dramatic highland landscapes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at Goðafoss waterfall — the 'Waterfall of the Gods' — one of Iceland's most spectacular and accessible waterfalls, right off the Ring Road. In winter it can be partially frozen, creating a magical scene. Continue south, stopping at Mývatn area for a brief look at the volcanic landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in the Geysir/Gullfoss area or continue to Reykjavik. Check into a mid-range guesthouse or hotel in the Reykjavik area (pre-booked). Dinner in Reykjavik to experience the capital's food scene.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — final breakfast before checkout
meals.lunch: Gamli Bærinn café near Mývatn — traditional Icelandic lamb soup and rye bread (budget ~2,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Reykjavik restaurant — Grillmarkaðurinn (Grill Market) for mid-range Icelandic cuisine; try the lamb or fish of the day (budget ~5,000–7,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day — start no later than 08:00 to arrive in Reykjavik before dark. The Ring Road in January can have ice and snow; drive carefully and check road.is throughout the journey. Goðafoss is unmissable and only requires a 15-minute stop. Book Reykjavik accommodation well in advance for January.

day_by_day.morning: Golden Circle day trip from Reykjavik. Start at Þingvellir National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet. Walk the Almannagjá gorge and learn about Iceland's ancient parliament (Alþingi). The winter landscape here is hauntingly beautiful.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the Geysir Geothermal Area — watch Strokkur geyser erupt every 5–10 minutes, shooting boiling water 20–30 meters into the air. Then continue to Gullfoss waterfall — Iceland's most famous waterfall, partially frozen in January and absolutely spectacular. The ice formations are extraordinary.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavik. Visit the Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring in Flúðir on the way back — Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a naturally heated geothermal pool surrounded by bubbling hot springs and geysers. A more authentic and less crowded alternative to the Blue Lagoon. Soak for 1–2 hours.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Reykjavik — included or nearby café
meals.lunch: Geysir Center café — lamb soup and Icelandic meat soup (budget ~2,500–3,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Flúðir village restaurant or back in Reykjavik — Messinn restaurant for Icelandic fish pan dishes (budget ~4,500–6,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Lagoon costs approximately 3,500 ISK per adult — book online in advance. Bring a towel and swimsuit. Þingvellir is free to enter (parking fee ~750 ISK). The Golden Circle is Iceland's most popular tourist route but in January crowds are manageable. Dress in waterproof layers for Gullfoss — the spray can be intense even in winter.

day_by_day.morning: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa experience. Pre-book the Comfort package (includes silica mud mask, algae mask, and a drink). The Blue Lagoon is located near Keflavik airport, about 45 minutes from Reykjavik. Arrive at your booked time slot (morning slots are less crowded). Soak in the iconic milky-blue 38–40°C geothermal waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Reykjavik by early afternoon. Explore the capital: walk Laugavegur shopping street, visit Hallgrímskirkja church (take the elevator to the top for panoramic views — 1,000 ISK), and explore the colorful old harbor district (Grandi).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Reykjavik's vibrant food and culture scene. Visit the Harpa Concert Hall for its stunning architecture and check the events calendar for any concerts. Dinner in the city center.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before Blue Lagoon — hotel or café (the lagoon has a restaurant but it's expensive)
meals.lunch: Blue Lagoon LAVA Restaurant — splurge on the lagoon-side dining experience; fish of the day or Icelandic lamb (budget ~6,000–8,000 ISK — this is a treat day)
meals.dinner: Snaps Bistro in Reykjavik — French-Icelandic fusion, excellent value; try the mussels or duck confit (budget ~4,500–6,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Blue Lagoon MUST be pre-booked online — it sells out weeks in advance, especially on weekends. The Comfort package costs approximately 12,990 ISK. Arrive 10 minutes before your slot. Silica mud is provided free at the lagoon. Remove all jewelry before entering as the minerals can damage metals. The lagoon is open from 08:00 in winter.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure at Þingvellir National Park. Join a guided snorkel tour between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates in crystal-clear glacial water (visibility up to 100 meters). The water is 2–4°C but dry suits are provided. A truly once-in-a-lifetime experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Silfra experience, warm up with hot chocolate and soup at the Þingvellir visitor center. Drive back toward Reykjavik via the Nesjavellir geothermal power plant — you can see the steam rising dramatically from the hillside. Stop at Hveragerði hot spring town for a short walk to the geothermal river valley (Reykjadalur).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavik. Visit the Settlement Exhibition (Landnámssýningin) — an underground museum built around a Viking longhouse discovered beneath the city. Excellent for understanding Iceland's history. Dinner in the city.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — eat well before the cold water experience
meals.lunch: Þingvellir visitor center café — hot soup and sandwiches to warm up after Silfra (budget ~2,000–2,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Fiskfélagið (Fish Company) in Reykjavik — creative Icelandic seafood in a cozy cellar setting (budget ~5,500–7,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Silfra snorkeling tours cost approximately 19,000–22,000 ISK per person — book well in advance through Dive.is or Arctic Adventures. You must be a confident swimmer. The dry suit keeps you warm but your face will be cold — this is normal. The Reykjadalur hot spring river hike is approximately 3km each way and can be muddy/icy in January — wear waterproof boots.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the South Coast. Drive east on Route 1 to Seljalandsfoss waterfall — you can walk behind this stunning 60-meter waterfall (may be icy/closed in January — check conditions). Continue to Skógafoss waterfall — equally impressive and more accessible in winter. Climb the 527 steps to the top for panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east to Vík í Mýrdal — Iceland's southernmost village. Walk to the black sand beach at Reynisfjara (with extreme caution — sneaker waves are deadly year-round). Admire the dramatic basalt columns and Reynisdrangar sea stacks. Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja-like Vík church on the hill.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Reykjavik, stopping at Seljalandsfoss for a different perspective in the evening light (if conditions allow). Return to Reykjavik for dinner. Another aurora watch opportunity on the drive back if skies are clear — pull over safely away from the road.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Reykjavik
meals.lunch: Skógar Museum café near Skógafoss — lamb soup and Icelandic meat dishes (budget ~2,500–3,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Suður-Vík restaurant in Vík or back in Reykjavik — Kol Restaurant for wood-fired Icelandic dishes (budget ~4,500–6,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: NEVER turn your back on the ocean at Reynisfjara — sneaker waves have killed tourists here. Stay well back from the waterline. Seljalandsfoss walkway behind the waterfall is often closed in winter due to ice — check locally. The South Coast is Iceland's most visited tourist corridor but in January it's relatively quiet. Total driving distance today is approximately 300km.

day_by_day.morning: Skaftafell Glacier Hike on Vatnajökull. This requires an early start and a longer drive (approximately 3 hours from Reykjavik to Skaftafell). Join a guided glacier hike with crampons across Europe's largest glacier. Expert guides from local operators (Glacier Guides or Arctic Adventures) lead you safely across the ice. Explore stunning ice formations, crevasses, and blue ice caves.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the glacier hike (typically 3–4 hours), visit the nearby Svartifoss waterfall in Skaftafell — a stunning black basalt column waterfall (short 1.5km hike). Warm up with hot drinks at the Skaftafell visitor center. Begin the drive back west.
day_by_day.evening: Stop at Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon on the way back if time permits — even in January, icebergs calve from the glacier into the lagoon and it's a magical sight. Return to Reykjavik late evening. Dinner at the hotel or a nearby restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast or packed breakfast to eat in the car
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or Skaftafell visitor center café — hot soup and sandwiches (budget ~2,000–2,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Reykjavik — Grillið restaurant at Radisson Blu Saga Hotel for a special evening meal with panoramic city views (budget ~6,000–8,500 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Glacier hike tours cost approximately 9,000–12,000 ISK per person — book well in advance. All equipment (crampons, harness, helmet) is provided. Minimum age is typically 10 years. The drive to Skaftafell is long — depart by 06:30 to make the morning tour. Jökulsárlón is approximately 30 minutes east of Skaftafell and absolutely worth the detour. This is a very full day — pace yourself.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. Depending on your departure flight time, enjoy a leisurely last breakfast in Reykjavik. Take a final walk along the Reykjavik waterfront (Sæbraut) and visit the Sun Voyager sculpture (Sólfar) — a beautiful stainless steel Viking ship sculpture by the sea. Browse Laugavegur for last-minute souvenirs: Icelandic wool sweaters (lopapeysa), skyr, licorice, and local design items.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Iceland (Þjóðminjasafn Íslands) if time allows — excellent overview of Icelandic history from settlement to modern times (2,000 ISK entry). Return rental car at Keflavik Airport (allow 45 minutes drive from Reykjavik plus 1 hour for car return and check-in). Depart Iceland with incredible memories.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Keflavik International Airport. Enjoy a final Icelandic meal at the airport — try the airport's Fiskmarkaðurinn or Pylsuvagninn for a classic Icelandic hot dog (pylsa) — a beloved local tradition.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — enjoy a full Icelandic spread one last time: skyr, smoked salmon, rye bread, eggs, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Café Paris or Bergsson Mathús in Reykjavik city center — open sandwiches and soup (budget ~2,500–3,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Keflavik Airport — Icelandic hot dog (pylsa) with all the toppings from the airport kiosk (~500 ISK) — the perfect farewell to Iceland

day_by_day.notes: Return the rental car with a full tank of fuel — fill up in Reykjavik before heading to the airport as fuel at the airport is more expensive. Allow extra time for car return procedures. The classic Icelandic hot dog (pylsa) with remoulade, raw onion, crispy onion, and mustard is a must-try before departure. Check your flight status on the Icelandair app. Ensure you have receipts for any VAT refund claims (minimum purchase 6,000 ISK per store).

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Iceland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunting Tour
experiences.description: Join a guided evening tour away from Reykjavik's light pollution to witness the aurora borealis dancing across the sky. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and you'll learn about the science behind this natural phenomenon while capturing stunning photographs.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and swim-up bars while surrounded by dramatic lava fields. Book the Comfort package for access to the main lagoon, towel rental, and one silica mud mask.

experiences.name: Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure
experiences.description: Snorkel or dive between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates in crystal-clear glacial water with visibility up to 100 meters. The surreal blue and green hues of the water make this one of the most unique natural experiences on Earth, guided by certified instructors.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring
experiences.description: Relax in Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a naturally heated geothermal pool surrounded by bubbling hot springs and a small geyser that erupts every few minutes. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic experience offers a peaceful soak amid stunning Icelandic countryside.

experiences.name: Skaftafell Glacier Hike on Vatnajökull
experiences.description: Strap on crampons and hike across Europe's largest glacier with an expert guide. Explore stunning ice formations, deep blue crevasses, and ash layers from ancient volcanic eruptions. The hike offers breathtaking panoramic views of the surrounding black sand plains and mountain peaks.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Keflavík International Airport at 06:10. Clear customs and collect luggage. Transfer via private luxury vehicle to Reykjavík for a brief rest and freshening up at a premium airport lounge or boutique hotel day-use room. Begin the scenic drive north toward Siglufjörður — approximately 5–6 hours with stops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop en route at Borgarnes for a warm lunch break. Continue north through the dramatic Héðinsfjörður tunnel and Tröllaskagi peninsula. Arrive at Hotel Siglunes in Siglufjörður by late afternoon. Check in, unpack, and settle into your premium room overlooking the fjord. Take a short stroll along the charming harbor to acclimate to the Arctic town.
day_by_day.evening: Quiet first evening at the hotel. Enjoy a welcome dinner at the hotel's restaurant featuring locally sourced Arctic char and lamb. Keep an eye on the sky for early northern lights activity — Siglufjörður's minimal light pollution makes it an excellent vantage point.

meals.breakfast: Light refreshments at Keflavík Airport lounge or packed premium snack box arranged by your transfer service
meals.lunch: Hyrnan Restaurant in Borgarnes — known for hearty Icelandic lamb soup and fresh fish dishes in a cozy setting
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes restaurant — Arctic char with dill butter, slow-roasted lamb shank, and Icelandic skyr dessert paired with local craft beer

day_by_day.notes: Given the very early arrival and long transfer drive, keep Day 1 relaxed. Pre-arrange private luxury transfer (e.g., Black Car Iceland or similar) from Keflavík. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance and request early check-in if possible. Pack layers for the drive — January temperatures along the route can drop well below 0°C.

day_by_day.morning: After a restorative night's sleep, enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Explore Siglufjörður's iconic Herring Era Museum (Síldarminjasafnið) — one of Iceland's finest regional museums, spread across three restored warehouses documenting the town's dramatic herring boom era. The museum offers a fascinating and immersive premium guided experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Lace up and take a guided snowshoe or winter hiking tour along the lower slopes above Siglufjörður. The surrounding mountains offer breathtaking views of the fjord below, snow-draped peaks, and the compact colorful townscape. Alternatively, arrange a private photography tour with a local guide to capture the dramatic winter light (golden hour lasts only a few hours in January).
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunting Tour — join a small-group or private guided evening excursion from Siglufjörður into the surrounding darkness of the Tröllaskagi peninsula. Your guide will monitor aurora forecasts and drive to optimal viewing spots away from any ambient light. Wrap up in provided thermal suits and sip hot cocoa under the dancing lights.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — Icelandic buffet with smoked salmon, rye bread, skyr with berries, and freshly brewed coffee
meals.lunch: Kaffi Rauðka in Siglufjörður — a beloved local café serving homemade soups, open-faced sandwiches, and excellent coffee in a warm, intimate atmosphere
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes — pan-seared cod with langoustine bisque, roasted root vegetables, and a curated Icelandic wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Aurora activity depends on clear skies and solar activity (KP index). Download the Vedur.is app and Aurora Forecast app to monitor conditions. January in Siglufjörður sees only 4–5 hours of daylight, so plan outdoor activities around the brief midday light window (roughly 11:00–15:00).

day_by_day.morning: Drive south along Route 76 and then Route 1 toward Akureyri — Iceland's 'Capital of the North,' approximately 1.5 hours from Siglufjörður. Explore Akureyri's charming town center: visit the striking Akureyrarkirkja church perched on the hill, browse the Akureyri Art Museum, and stroll the pedestrian Hafnarstræti street lined with boutique shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Akureyri Botanical Garden (Lystigarðurinn) — the world's northernmost botanical garden, serene and frost-covered in winter. Then head to the nearby Kjarnaskógur forest for a peaceful winter walk among Iceland's rare woodland. Return to Siglufjörður via the scenic coastal road, stopping at viewpoints over Eyjafjörður.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at one of Akureyri's finest restaurants before returning to Siglufjörður, or return first and dine at the hotel. Another aurora watch from the hotel terrace or a short drive to a dark-sky spot near town.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — eggs Benedict with smoked lamb, fresh pastries, and Icelandic dairy
meals.lunch: Rub23 in Akureyri — a celebrated restaurant known for creative sushi and premium Icelandic seafood with Asian fusion influences
meals.dinner: Strikið Restaurant in Akureyri — rooftop dining with panoramic fjord views, featuring dry-aged Icelandic beef, langoustine, and an extensive wine list (reserve in advance)

day_by_day.notes: Akureyri is a worthwhile day trip from Siglufjörður. Roads in January can be icy — if not driving yourself, arrange a private driver for the day. Akureyri Airport also offers domestic flights if you wish to adjust the itinerary later.

day_by_day.morning: Full day excursion to the Mývatn region — approximately 1.5 hours east of Akureyri (2.5 hours from Siglufjörður). Depart early and visit the extraordinary Dimmuborgir lava field, a surreal landscape of twisted volcanic pillars and caves. Explore the Hverfjall tephra crater rim for sweeping views across the frozen lake.
day_by_day.afternoon: Soak in the Mývatn Nature Baths (Jarðböðin við Mývatn) — often called the 'Blue Lagoon of the North,' these geothermal pools sit at 36–40°C amid a dramatic volcanic landscape. The premium experience includes private changing facilities, in-water relaxation, and silica mud masks. Afterward, visit the Námaskarð geothermal area with its bubbling mud pools and steaming fumaroles.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siglufjörður. Enjoy a quiet, restorative dinner at the hotel. If skies are clear, set an alarm for peak aurora hours (typically 22:00–02:00) and step outside for a private northern lights viewing from the hotel's waterfront location.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — continental spread with Icelandic cheeses, cold cuts, and fresh juice
meals.lunch: Vogafjós Farm Resort near Mývatn — a unique farm restaurant serving fresh geothermal rye bread baked underground, homemade cheese, and lamb directly from their own farm
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes — slow-cooked reindeer stew with root vegetable purée and cloudberry compote

day_by_day.notes: Mývatn Nature Baths are less crowded than the Blue Lagoon and equally spectacular. Book entry in advance. The drive to Mývatn via Route 1 is stunning but can be challenging in winter — check road conditions at road.is before departing. Consider hiring a local guide or driver for this excursion.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Tröllaskagi peninsula close to Siglufjörður. Take a private guided snowmobile or super-jeep tour into the highlands above the town, accessing terrain inaccessible by regular vehicle. The views from the mountain ridges over multiple fjords are extraordinary in winter light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the neighboring village of Ólafsfjörður (20 minutes south through the tunnel) and explore its small but charming harbor. Stop at the local swimming pool (sundlaug) for a warm geothermal soak — a quintessential Icelandic experience. Return to Siglufjörður and spend time at the hotel's spa facilities if available, or relax with a book by the fire.
day_by_day.evening: Private Northern Lights experience — arrange with a local guide for a dedicated aurora hunt by super-jeep into the mountains above Siglufjörður. The elevation and complete darkness offer exceptional viewing conditions. Champagne and warm refreshments included in the premium package.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — smoked salmon on sourdough, poached eggs, and freshly squeezed juice
meals.lunch: Packed premium picnic lunch prepared by the hotel for the snowmobile/super-jeep tour — thermos of soup, artisan sandwiches, and Icelandic chocolate
meals.dinner: Hotel Siglunes — pan-seared halibut with saffron cream, asparagus, and potato gratin, paired with a crisp white Burgundy

day_by_day.notes: Snowmobile tours require a valid driver's license. Super-jeep tours are available for non-drivers. January snowpack in the Tröllaskagi mountains is typically excellent. Book adventure tours through local operators such as Arctic Adventures North or Siglufjörður-based guides.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Siglufjörður and begin the journey south toward the Golden Circle region. Drive via Route 1 south through Akureyri and continue toward the interior. Stop at Goðafoss waterfall — the 'Waterfall of the Gods' — one of Iceland's most dramatic and accessible waterfalls, particularly stunning with winter ice formations along its edges.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue south and check into a luxury property near the Golden Circle area (e.g., Ion Adventure Hotel near Þingvellir or a premium guesthouse near Geysir). Visit the Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring in Flúðir — Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a naturally heated geothermal pool surrounded by bubbling hot springs and steaming geysers. The intimate, rustic atmosphere is far more authentic than larger commercial pools.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at the Ion Adventure Hotel's Silfra Restaurant (if staying there) — one of Iceland's most acclaimed fine dining experiences, featuring a tasting menu of hyper-local Icelandic ingredients with stunning views of the lava fields and potential aurora activity through floor-to-ceiling windows.

meals.breakfast: Hotel Siglunes — final breakfast before departure; full Icelandic spread
meals.lunch: Fosshótel Húsavík or a roadside stop near Goðafoss — lamb burger or fish and chips with local beer
meals.dinner: Silfra Restaurant at Ion Adventure Hotel — multi-course tasting menu featuring fermented shark, smoked lamb, and Arctic herbs (advance reservation essential)

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day (approximately 5–6 hours total). Consider breaking it up with the Goðafoss stop and a leisurely lunch. The Secret Lagoon in Flúðir is open year-round and far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon — book tickets in advance. Road conditions on Route 1 in January require careful monitoring.

day_by_day.morning: Golden Circle exploration — visit Þingvellir National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet and where Iceland's first parliament (Alþingi) was established in 930 AD. Walk the Almannagjá rift valley with a private guide who can explain the geological and historical significance in depth.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkeling or Diving in Silfra Fissure — the crown jewel of Þingvellir. Don a dry suit and slip between the two tectonic plates in water of extraordinary clarity (visibility up to 100 meters). The water temperature is 2–4°C year-round, but the dry suit keeps you comfortable. This is a once-in-a-lifetime experience. Afterward, visit the Geysir geothermal area to watch Strokkur erupt every 5–10 minutes.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to Gullfoss waterfall for a dramatic twilight or early evening visit — the 'Golden Falls' are spectacular in winter, often partially frozen with ice formations. Return to your Golden Circle accommodation for a celebratory dinner.

meals.breakfast: Ion Adventure Hotel or accommodation — premium buffet with Icelandic dairy, fresh pastries, and hot porridge
meals.lunch: Geysir Center Restaurant — warm lamb soup and fresh bread after the Silfra dive, essential for rewarming
meals.dinner: Friðheimar Tomato Farm Restaurant near Reykholt — a unique greenhouse dining experience where you eat surrounded by growing tomato plants; tomato-based menu with fresh produce and Icelandic lamb

day_by_day.notes: Silfra snorkeling/diving requires advance booking through a certified operator (e.g., DIVE.IS or Arctic Adventures). Snorkeling requires no certification; diving requires Open Water certification. Dry suits are provided. The experience lasts approximately 3 hours including briefing and gearing up. Water temperature is extreme — follow all guide instructions.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to the Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa — pre-book the premium Retreat Spa package, which includes private changing suites, in-water floating massage, silica and algae mask treatments, and access to the exclusive Retreat Lagoon (a quieter, more intimate section of the lagoon). Arrive early to enjoy the experience before crowds build.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Blue Lagoon experience through the afternoon. Enjoy the in-water bar, lava restaurant, and steam caves. The milky-blue 38–40°C waters are rich in silica, algae, and minerals — deeply restorative after days of winter exploration. Depart mid-afternoon refreshed and rejuvenated.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a luxury Reykjavík hotel (e.g., The Retreat at Blue Lagoon, Hotel Borg, or 101 Hotel) for the final nights. Explore Reykjavík's vibrant Laugavegur street in the evening. Dinner at one of the capital's finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Accommodation near Golden Circle — light breakfast before the drive to Blue Lagoon
meals.lunch: LAVA Restaurant at Blue Lagoon — dine in your bathrobe with views over the lagoon; Icelandic seafood platter, langoustine soup, and skyr cheesecake
meals.dinner: Dill Restaurant in Reykjavík — Iceland's first Michelin-starred restaurant, offering a Nordic tasting menu celebrating Icelandic terroir (advance reservation essential, book weeks ahead)

day_by_day.notes: Blue Lagoon Retreat Spa packages must be booked well in advance — they sell out months ahead, especially on weekends. The Retreat package costs significantly more than standard entry but offers an incomparably luxurious experience. Bring or purchase high-quality hair conditioner as the silica water can be drying.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Reykjavík's cultural highlights: visit Hallgrímskirkja church and take the elevator to the top for panoramic city views. Walk to the Harpa Concert Hall on the waterfront — an architectural masterpiece of geometric glass panels. Browse the Settlement Exhibition (Landnámssýningin) — an underground museum built around a Viking-age longhouse.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Iceland for a comprehensive overview of Icelandic history and culture. Explore the Tjörnin lake area and the colorful old town streets. Stop at a premium Icelandic design boutique for souvenirs — look for Icelandic wool (lopapeysa sweaters), handcrafted jewelry, and artisan food products.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunting Tour from Reykjavík — join a premium small-group tour by super-jeep to locations outside the city where light pollution is minimal. Expert guides monitor aurora forecasts in real time and drive to optimal locations. Hot drinks and thermal blankets provided.

meals.breakfast: Reykjavík luxury hotel — full breakfast buffet with Icelandic specialties
meals.lunch: Messinn Restaurant in Reykjavík — celebrated for its cast-iron pan-cooked fish dishes; the seafood pan is exceptional
meals.dinner: Grillið Restaurant at Radisson Blu Saga Hotel — rooftop fine dining with city views, featuring premium Icelandic beef, lamb, and an extensive wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Reykjavík is very walkable — most city center attractions are within 15–20 minutes on foot. January evenings in Reykjavík can be windy and wet — dress in waterproof layers. The northern lights are visible from Reykjavík on very clear nights, but a dedicated tour significantly improves your chances.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the South Coast — depart Reykjavík early by private vehicle or guided tour. Drive along the Ring Road to Seljalandsfoss waterfall, where you can walk behind the curtain of falling water (may be icy in January — exercise caution). Continue to Skógafoss waterfall, equally dramatic with potential ice formations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east to the black sand beach of Reynisfjara near Vík — one of the world's most dramatic beaches, with towering basalt columns, sea stacks (Reynisdrangar), and powerful Atlantic waves. Exercise extreme caution with sneaker waves. Visit the charming village of Vík and the Reyniskirkja church on the hill for panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavík. Enjoy a relaxed evening with dinner at a premium restaurant. If aurora forecast is favorable, take a short drive outside the city for another viewing opportunity.

meals.breakfast: Reykjavík hotel — full breakfast before early departure
meals.lunch: Skál! at Hlemmur Mathöll food hall in Reykjavík (on return) or a packed premium lunch for the road — alternatively, Black Beach Restaurant near Reynisfjara for local fish and lamb
meals.dinner: Fiskfélagið (Fish Company) in Reykjavík — creative Icelandic seafood in a historic cellar setting; the tasting menu is exceptional

day_by_day.notes: The South Coast drive is approximately 2.5 hours each way from Reykjavík. Reynisfjara beach is beautiful but genuinely dangerous — never turn your back on the ocean. January road conditions on Route 1 south of Reykjavík are generally good but can be icy. Check road.is before departing.

day_by_day.morning: Skaftafell Glacier Hike on Vatnajökull — this requires an early departure from Reykjavík (approximately 3.5–4 hours drive to Skaftafell). Strap on crampons and hike across Europe's largest glacier with a certified expert guide. Explore stunning ice formations, crevasses, and blue ice caves. The experience is otherworldly and physically exhilarating.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the glacier hike, visit the nearby Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon — one of Iceland's most iconic landscapes. Watch icebergs calve from the Breiðamerkurjökull glacier and drift through the lagoon. Walk to Diamond Beach where translucent ice chunks wash up on black sand. In winter, the lagoon is often partially frozen, creating an ethereal atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Given the distance, consider staying overnight near Jökulsárlón at a premium guesthouse (e.g., Fosshotel Glacier Lagoon) rather than returning to Reykjavík. Dinner at the hotel restaurant with views of the glacier. Aurora viewing from the lagoon shore — one of Iceland's most spectacular aurora backdrops.

meals.breakfast: Reykjavík hotel — early breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Packed premium lunch on the glacier (provided by tour operator) — hot soup in a thermos, energy bars, and warm drinks
meals.dinner: Fosshotel Glacier Lagoon restaurant — locally sourced lamb and fish with glacier views; or Hótel Skaftafell restaurant for hearty Icelandic cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Glacier hiking requires advance booking with a certified operator (e.g., Icelandic Mountain Guides or Local Guide). Minimum fitness level required. All equipment (crampons, helmets, harnesses) is provided. This is a full-day excursion — plan for 10–12 hours away from Reykjavík. Staying overnight near Jökulsárlón is strongly recommended to avoid a very long return drive in the dark.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon at dawn for photography — the early morning light (around 10:30–11:00 in January) on the icebergs is extraordinary. Take a final walk on Diamond Beach. Begin the drive back toward Reykjavík, stopping at Skógafoss and Seljalandsfoss again if conditions differ from the previous visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Reykjavík by mid-afternoon. Spend the afternoon at leisure — visit the Reykjavík Art Museum (Kjarvalsstaðir) for Icelandic contemporary art, or indulge in a premium spa treatment at your hotel. Browse Laugavegur for last-minute luxury souvenirs: Icelandic design, Geysir wool products, and artisan spirits.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at one of Reykjavík's most celebrated restaurants. Final aurora watch from a rooftop or a short drive outside the city if conditions permit.

meals.breakfast: Fosshotel Glacier Lagoon — full breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Roadside stop at Selfoss or Hveragerði — Ölverk Pizza & Brewery in Hveragerði for artisan pizza and geothermally brewed beer in a unique setting
meals.dinner: Óx Restaurant in Reykjavík — an ultra-exclusive 12-seat chef's table experience offering a surprise tasting menu of Icelandic ingredients (book months in advance); alternatively, Matur og Drykkur for traditional Icelandic recipes reimagined with modern technique

day_by_day.notes: The return drive from Jökulsárlón to Reykjavík is approximately 4 hours. Depart by 09:00 to make the most of the brief daylight. Hveragerði is a geothermal town worth a brief stop — you can see steam rising from the ground throughout the town. Confirm your departure flight details and arrange airport transfer for the following morning.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Reykjavík. Enjoy a leisurely last breakfast at your hotel. If time permits before airport transfer, take a final walk along the Sæbraut coastal path with views of Mount Esja across the bay. Visit the Sun Voyager (Sólfarið) sculpture on the waterfront — a beautiful symbol of Iceland's seafaring heritage and a perfect final image of the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart for Keflavík International Airport via private luxury transfer (approximately 45 minutes). Allow ample time for check-in and security. Browse the Duty Free store for Icelandic spirits (Brennivín, Icelandic gin), Nói Síríus chocolate, and premium Icelandic skincare products from the Blue Lagoon range.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Keflavík International Airport. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of northern lights, geothermal wonders, glaciers, and the raw, elemental beauty of Iceland.

meals.breakfast: Reykjavík luxury hotel — full final breakfast; savor every last bite of Icelandic skyr and smoked salmon
meals.lunch: Keflavík Airport — Fiskmarkaðurinn (Fish Market) airport outlet or premium airport lounge dining
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange your private airport transfer the night before and confirm pickup time. Keflavík Airport is 50 km from Reykjavík — allow at least 2 hours before departure for international flights. The Icelandair Saga Lounge at Keflavík offers premium seating, hot food, and drinks for business class passengers. Consider purchasing travel insurance that covers weather-related disruptions, which are common in Iceland in January.
